article.title: Mayor opens book fair at Empress Market
article.summary: KARACHI: Karachi Mayor Murtaza Wahab on Saturday inaugurated a book fair at the Empress Market, turning a once-encroached public space into a venue for books, cultural events and community activities.Wahab said the nearly 150-year-old heritage site had been restored after the removal of encroachments and would now be used as a cultural centre and public space.“Citizens should visit Empress Market, buy books and support local publishers,” Wahab said while speaking at the inauguration of the fair, titled “Kitabon Ka Jahan” (World of Books).He said books were an important source of knowledge, awareness and positive thinking, and that promoting reading among young people was essential for building an educated and tolerant society.Wahab visited the bookstalls and bought several books himself. article.title: Karachi police book 3 over alleged abduction of young man in DHA
article.summary: KARACHI: Police on Saturday registered a case against three named suspects over the alleged physical assault of a young man in the Defence Housing Authority’s (DHA) Phase 8.The first information report (FIR), a copy of which is available withDawn, was registered at Sahil police station in the early hours of Saturday on the complaint of Syed Ali Jafri. According to the FIR, the incident took place on the night of Aug 29.The FIR invoked sections 34 (acts done by several persons), 337-A(i) (punishment ofshajjah), 337-V(arshfor hair), 365 (kidnapping or abducting with intent secretly and wrongfully to confine person) and 506-B (criminal intimidation if threat be to cause death or grievous hurt) of thePakistan Penal Code(PPC).Jafri also spoke to the media on Saturday,recallingdetails of the incident and explaining that the “delay” in getting the FIR registered was because he had been threatened by the suspects against doing so.In his complaint, Jafri said he “remained silent” after the i...

article.title: SMOKERS’ CORNER: A SEPARATE PROVINCE?
article.summary: The debate over whether Karachi should beseparatedfrom the province of Sindh is one of the oldest in Pakistan. On one side, the Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) argues that Karachi is the heart of Sindh. On the other side, parties representing the Urdu-speaking Mohajir population, such as the Muttahida Qaumi Movement (MQM), argue that Karachi is neglected because it does not have a Sindhi majority.The MQM views the PPP as a ‘Sindhi party’, even though, till 2008, the PPP had an impressive vote bank in the country’s largest province, Punjab, and currently it is the ruling party in Balochistan and Gilgit-Baltistan, apart from, of course, Sindh.Karachi’s Mohajir population, whose political support is distributed primarily among the MQM, the Jamaat-i-Islami (JI) and the Pakistan Tehreek-i-Insaf (PTI), believes the city can only improve if it becomes its own separate province or falls under federal control.Most political commentators describe this as a conflict between Sindhis and Mohajirs. ...
